svg.title: Four stages, two curves, and the gap between them
svg.desc: Top: the demographic transition drawn properly. The two rates fall one after the other, not together, and the shaded gap between them is the population boom. That is the whole model: mortality falls first because sanitation, food and basic medicine are cheap and need no change in behaviour; fertility falls later because it requires urbanisation, schooling for girls, contraception and a change in what children are for. Bottom left: the three pyramid shapes and what each predicts. Bottom right: the measures, with the trap that catches most people — a crude rate is not adjusted for age, so two populations with different age structures cannot be compared on one.
svg.text: Four stages, two curves, and the gap between them
Population grows in the gap — after deaths fall and before births follow
a proposed STAGE 5: births fall below deaths and the population shrinks — Japan, Korea, much of eastern Europe
the epidemiological transition runs alongside it: infection and famine → chronic degenerative disease
children per woman at current rates
a retirement town has a high crude death rate
rates, or the comparison means nothing.
